title: Cultural participation is strongly age- and disability-stratified across Europe
source_unit: Eurostat, ilc_scp37 cultural or sport participation dataset, 2022 EU-SILC quality-of-life module; 2026 culture-statistics refresh
geography: European countries in the Eurostat dataset; selected comparative cells and Sweden subgroup cells

observations.period: 2022; people aged 16 or over; at least once in the prior 12 months

denominator.unit: Eurostat percentage universe for each country; national population aged 16 or over, not a reported respondent count

cultural_activity_any.value: Sweden 62.9%; Netherlands 68.9%; Ireland 61.9%; Belgium 59.2%; Spain 58.5%; France 54.4%; Italy 36.9%; Bulgaria 19.7%; Türkiye 19.4%
cultural_activity_any.unit: percent participating at least once in cinema, live performances, or cultural sites

mechanism.value: Cultural participation is not a single European consumer norm; country-level access, supply, income, transport, institutions, and measurement context produce wide participation gradients

observations.method: Eurostat EU-SILC quality-of-life cultural-participation indicator; harmonized country percentages by activity, frequency, disability limitation, sex, and age.
observations.uncertainty: The dataset reports percentages rather than a common pooled respondent denominator in the API extract; national fieldwork and cultural supply contexts differ, and cross-country gaps are descriptive rather than causal.
observations.subgroup: People aged 16 or over, total sex and disability category; selected countries.
observations.counterinterpretation: A lower reported participation rate can reflect different cultural definitions, supply, survey mode, recall, or frequency thresholds rather than lower cultural value or social connection.

observations.period: 2022; Sweden; people aged 16 or over; at least once in the prior 12 months

denominator.unit: Swedish population aged 16 or over in the Eurostat percentage universe

cultural_activity_any_total.unit: percent participating at least once in cinema, live performances, or cultural sites

cultural_activity_any_no_limitation.unit: percent among people reporting no activity limitation

cultural_activity_any_some_limitation.unit: percent among people reporting some activity limitation

cultural_activity_any_severe_limitation.unit: percent among people reporting severe activity limitation

mechanism.value: Disability limitation is associated with a large cultural-participation gradient even in a high-participation country, making accessibility, transport, venue design, health, and support capacity central conversion conditions

observations.method: Eurostat EU-SILC quality-of-life cultural-participation indicator for Sweden, cross-tabulated by activity limitation severity.
observations.uncertainty: These are cross-sectional descriptive percentages; disability limitation is self-reported and the cells do not identify whether barriers arise from cost, transport, venue access, health, caregiving, preference, or supply.
observations.subgroup: Swedish residents aged 16 or over by self-reported activity limitation.
observations.counterinterpretation: The gradient may reflect health, age, income, transport, household support, and selection jointly; it is not an estimated causal disability effect.

observations.period: 2022; Sweden; people aged 16 or over; at least once in the prior 12 months

denominator.unit: Swedish population aged 16 or over in the Eurostat percentage universe

mechanism.value: Cultural participation falls across age bands, so cultural demand and social infrastructure should be read through life stage, health, mobility, digital access, and venue design rather than treated as a stable population trait

observations.method: Eurostat EU-SILC quality-of-life cultural-participation indicator for Sweden, cross-tabulated by age.
observations.uncertainty: The age gradient is descriptive and may combine cohort, health, income, transport, household composition, and cultural-supply differences; the 2022 module is not a longitudinal panel.
observations.subgroup: Swedish residents aged 16 or over by age band.
observations.counterinterpretation: Older adults may participate in activities not captured by this combined indicator or may face different frequency and access patterns; lower attendance is not equivalent to lower cultural engagement.

boundary: This record adds harmonized cultural-participation evidence connecting country context, disability limitation, and age to reported participation in cinema, live performances, or cultural sites. It is a 2022 cross-sectional percentage dataset refreshed and documented in 2026, not a causal accessibility estimate, a longitudinal participation record, a spending measure, or proof of cultural belonging or wellbeing.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Official Eurostat API extract reviewed for dataset dimensions, labels, 2022 values, Sweden disability and age cells, selected-country comparison cells, and percentage-universe limitations.
